clue.text: Go by number reverting to one type of pizza

parts.note: go, as in energy or vigour, is pep
per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: reverting means turning back, so the word for number is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a pizza by its menu number keeps coming back to the same one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pepperoni pizza is a familiar variety, topped with spicy sausage slices.

clue.text: Ring, interrupting old Northerner, a bit loopy

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the ring letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: An ancient northerner is being called slightly crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loopy' looks like slang for mad, but a picot is literally a small loop of thread on lace edging.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a tiny ornamental loop worked along the edge of lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Lateral thinking may or may not help with how to fit this solution in

definitions.text: Lateral thinking may or may not help with how to fit this solution in

parts.words: Lateral thinking may or may not help with how to fit this solution in
parts.note: a down entry runs vertically in the grid, at right angles to lateral (sideways) thinking, so the clue describes the way the word is written in

explanation.surface: A puzzler wonders whether creative thinking will help slot this answer into the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A down entry is written vertically, at right angles to the horizontal rows.

clue.text: Catch up with the half-time scores?

definitions.text: Catch up with the half-time scores?

parts.words: Catch up with the half-time scores?
parts.note: reads like checking on match news, but means drawing level, making the scores the same

explanation.surface: A fan wants to hear the half-time football results.
explanation.definitionFit: To level the score in a game is to draw level with the opponent, catching them up.

clue.text: Single basic skill involved in French department

indicators.note: involved in means set inside, so the skill letter goes within the word for single

parts.note: single means one
the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic) are the basic skills, so one R stands for a basic skill

explanation.surface: Someone notes a single basic skill being taught in a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orne is a department of Normandy in north-west France, named after its river.

clue.text: Villain with OBE out of order -it should be sacrosanct

indicators.note: out of order means not in the right sequence, so these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rogue honoured with an OBE is scandalous, since the honour ought to be beyond reproach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' looks like a judgement on the honour, but it signals rearranging the letters of VILLAIN plus OBE (Order of the British Empire, a British honour).
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacrosanct is too sacred to be violated, which is exactly what this adjective says.

clue.text: Market-place in La Paz, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests a rearranged version of the letters of the city name

explanation.surface: An open market square in the Bolivian capital is pictured.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is a public square or open market area in a Spanish-speaking town.

clue.text: Mess made of G&S? Shame about that

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for shame goes around the other letters

parts.note: shame, as in 'what a shame', means pity
G&S is the usual short form of Gilbert and Sullivan, the comic opera partnership

explanation.surface: Someone laments a bungled production of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigsty is figuratively any filthy, untidy place, a real mess.

clue.text: In the running, with two to go?

definitions.text: In the running, with two to go?

parts.words: In the running, with two to go?
parts.note: reads like a contender in a race, but describes position in a sequence: third from the end, with two more still to come

explanation.surface: A contender is still in the race with two rounds remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means third from last, so in a running order two items follow it.

clue.text: The point of a simple missile's design

definitions.text: The point of a simple missile's design

parts.words: The point of a simple missile's design
parts.note: reads like the purpose of a weapon's design, but describes the pointed tip of an arrow, a simple missile, also a common design shape

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a basic projectile was designed for.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tip of an arrow is its point, and the same shape is a familiar design motif.

clue.text: Vicar touring Cam, on a ramble, and Chichester, once

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A clergyman goes walking around the River Cam, and Chichester gets a mention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touring' looks like a container signal around Cam, but it is part of the anagram: VICAR, TOURING and CAM together rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Chichester sailed single-handed round the world in 1966-67, a famous sailor of the globe.

clue.text: Player getting high on the pitch

definitions.text: Player getting high on the pitch

parts.words: Player getting high on the pitch
parts.note: reads like a footballer on a sports field, but describes a performer singing high notes, the pitch being musical

explanation.surface: A footballer seems to be getting intoxicated during the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy chorister singing the top part is known by this term for the highest vocal line.

clue.text: Bridge player's hand revealed — suggesting the right lead?

parts.note: in bridge the four players are named North, South, East and West
a paw is a hand, informally

explanation.surface: At the card table a player's hand is exposed, and the right card to lead is hinted at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a card led at bridge, but it is a boxer's leading hand: a left-handed boxer leads with the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-handed boxer stands with the right fist forward, leading with the right.

clue.text: Result of togetherness, when short day finishes with it

parts.note: FRI is the usual short form of Friday
finishes means ends
with it means fashionable, which is hip

explanation.surface: A pleasant shared time follows when a shortened working day closes in style.
explanation.definitionFit: A close bond between companions grows out of spending time together.

clue.text: Uninspired styling of town precinct?

definitions.meaning: a traffic-free shopping street is styled with this word, as in a ______ precinct

explanation.surface: A dull design for a town shopping area is criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull, ordinary piece of work is called this, and a car-free shopping zone carries the same word.

clue.text: There's a caveat before one's translation appears

definitions.text: There's a caveat before one's translation appears

parts.words: There's a caveat before one's translation appears
parts.note: the Latin phrase caveat emptor means let the buyer beware, so the word following caveat, translated, gives the answer

explanation.surface: A warning is issued before some translated text is published.
explanation.walkthrough: Caveat emptor is a well-known Latin legal maxim: 'let the buyer beware'. Emptor comes after caveat, and in English it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptor is Latin for a buyer, one who acquires goods by paying for them.

clue.text: Previously had to appear by eleven, in Madrid

definitions.meaning: previously means formerly, at one time
the Spanish word for the number eleven

explanation.surface: Someone once had to turn up before eleven o'clock in Madrid.
explanation.definitionFit: The English adverb means formerly, and the same spelling is Spanish for eleven.

clue.text: Untroubled about appearing twice in resturant

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so each RE goes into the word for restaurant
appearing twice says the word about is used a second time, also placed inside the restaurant word

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant
RE means about or concerning
the same word about supplies RE a second time, as the clue says it appears twice

explanation.surface: A diner is relaxed about turning up at the same eatery twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appearing twice' and 'in' put RE (about) into CAFE at two separate points, so the restaurant word is split twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone free of care or worry is untroubled.

clue.text: Music used to soothe baby

definitions.meaning: a genre of loud popular music with a strong beat
to sway a baby gently back and forth to calm it

explanation.surface: Gentle music is played to calm an infant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a popular music genre and also the gentle swaying motion that calms an infant.

clue.text: Given scolding -—had "ukelele' regarded as spelling error

indicators.note: a spelling error has the letters in the wrong order, so the letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was told off for writing a ukulele as a misspelt word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ukelele' is itself a common misspelling of ukulele, which makes the surface plausible; the letters of HAD and UKELELE rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dragged under a ship's keel was a naval punishment, and figuratively means being severely rebuked.

clue.text: Woman in church after New Year's Day

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the church letters follow the date

parts.note: New Year's Day is January 1, written JAN I
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A woman goes to church after the New Year holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Janice is a woman's first name, and any woman's name can be clued this way.

clue.text: End up, during brief vacation, hitting the old gin

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the landing word goes inside the holiday word

parts.note: HOLS is short for holidays, a British word for vacation
to end up somewhere is to land there

explanation.surface: A traveller arrives on a short break and starts drinking old-fashioned gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollands is an old name for Dutch gin, also called genever.

clue.text: Nothing about stuffing marrow perhaps seen as a nuisance

indicators.note: stuffing means filling, so the reversed word goes inside the vegetable word

parts.note: a marrow is a large vegetable, so it is an example of veg

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the slang word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Having nothing to stuff a marrow with is seen as annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: A marrow is a large squash, a common British vegetable. 'About' reverses the slang for nothing to XIN, and 'stuffing' fills the vegetable with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vexing is annoying, behaving as a nuisance does; the clue's 'seen as' bridges noun and adjective.

clue.text: Great poem contained inserted material

indicators.note: contained means held inside, so the poem goes within the letters for great

parts.note: GT is short for gran turismo, a 'grand touring' car, taken here as great
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A great poem had extra material added to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A godet is a triangular piece of fabric inserted into a skirt or sleeve to add fullness.

clue.text: No longer keen on a traditional king

parts.note: to go off something is to stop liking it

explanation.surface: Someone has lost interest in an old-fashioned monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famed for the earthwork Offa's Dyke.

clue.text: Honest skill held back, in view of rejected right charge

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the reversed skill goes within the view word

parts.note: sight means view

indicators.note: held back means reversed, so the word for skill is read backwards

parts.note: art means skill

indicators.note: rejected means turned away, so the little word of is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a ward is someone in another's charge

explanation.surface: A frank person suppresses their skill in light of a wrongly refused fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held back' gives TRA and 'in' places it within the view word; 'rejected' gives FO. 'In view of' looks like one phrase meaning FOR, but it splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A straightforward person is frank and honest, without deceit.

clue.text: Match the last word in poetry

definitions.meaning: to match in sound, as two line endings do
the echoing final word of a verse line

explanation.surface: Someone seeks the perfect closing word for a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that match in sound are said to do this, and the matching end word of a verse line is one.

clue.text: Mount comeback, to strengthen position

indicators.note: comeback means going back, so the mountain word is read backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
to cement is to strengthen or bind firmly

explanation.surface: A sports team mounts a comeback to secure its league position.
explanation.definitionFit: A placement is a position or posting, such as a job placement.
